subject: general
question: Ravi started a business by investing ₹ 50,000. After six months, Raju joined his business by investing ₹ 1,00,000. In the one year since Ravi invested, they earned a profit of ₹63,000. What is Raju's share in the profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Profit sharing ratio** = (Investment × Time) ratio

**Ravi : Raju** = (50,000 × 12) : (1,00,000 × 6)

**Ravi : Raju** = 6,00,000 : 6,00,000 = 1 : 1

Since the ratio is 1 : 1, the profit is divided **equally**.

**Raju profit share** = ₹63,000 ÷ 2 = ₹31,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹31,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Investment of Ravi** = ₹50,000 | **Time period** = 12 months

**Investment of Raju** = ₹1,00,000 | **Time period** = 6 months (Joined after 6 months)

**Total Annual Profit** = ₹63,000

**Formula Used:**

Profit Ratio = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf357a50433f05e0b865ec88da2dbe5d8878ea11aa0cd465a0640fda81667891.png] 

⇒ Ravi profit equivalent = 50,000 × 12 = 6,00,000

⇒ Raju profit equivalent = 1,00,000 × 6 = 6,00,000

⇒ Profit Ratio (Ravi : Raju) = 6,00,000 : 6,00,000

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 1

⇒ Total Ratio Parts = 1 + 1 = 2 units

⇒ 2 units = ₹63,000

⇒ 1 unit = ₹63,000 ÷ 2 = ₹31,500

⇒ Raju share (1 unit) = ₹31,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹31,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Profit Rule

In any business partnership, the **Profit (P)** is directly proportional to the product of **Capital (C)** and **Time (T)**. Formula: P₁ : P₂ = C₁T₁ : C₂T₂.

Types of Partners

An **Active Partner** manages the business and may take a salary before profit distribution, while a **Sleeping Partner** only provides capital.

Compound Partnership

When partners invest different amounts for different durations of time, it is called a **compound partnership**, where effective capital is calculated per unit of time.
